customer_xyz: Hey team — a customer is hitting truncated JSON when using streaming chat with JSON mode. They see the final '}' missing and a client-side parse error. Crashes their consumer app.
 eve_support: Thanks for flagging. Can you paste the raw stream snippet and the request headers? Also which SDK/version?
 customer_xyz: Using our node-client v3.2.1. Repro steps below. We call /v1/chat/stream with application/json; mode=structured. Response ends like this:
 ```
 data: {\n  \"choices\": [\n    {\"delta\": {\"content\": \"{\\\"id\\\": \"123\", \"items\": [\\\"a\\\", \\\"b\\\"]}\"}}\n  ]\n}\n\ndata: [DONE]\n ```
 But sometimes final chunk is just `data: {` or the `}` is missing. Downstream JSON.parse throws.
 mike_eng: Interesting. Any proxies between client and our edge? Chunk boundaries can be split by proxies. Also did you see any 401/403 midstream? If auth refresh happens it can close the connection.
 tara_infra: CI deploy bot recorded a connection close at the same time for one of these sessions. @ci_deploybot can you dump the logs?
 ci_deploybot: deploy-bastion: saw tcp FIN from client IP 52.12.34.56 at 1969998908. Upstream responded 200 until byte offset 14,532 then connection closed. No 401 on server.
 customer_xyz: We do rotate tokens via a refresh flow. Token refresh happens on the client about every 30s. The stream is long (several minutes). Maybe the client is re-opening sockets.
 eve_support: Two hypotheses: 1) Client-side token refresh triggers a reconnect that tears midstream, leaving partial last JSON event. 2) Intermediate proxy or HTTP/2 multiplexing splits chunk at a bad boundary. Can you confirm whether you're using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2?
 customer_xyz: HTTP/2 with browser Fetch + service worker intercept. Repro steps: open stream, after ~45s trigger refresh, observe partial last event ~30% of runs.
 mike_eng: OK can you try forcing HTTP/1.1 (curl --http1.1) and see if it reproduces? Also capture exact sequence of SSE frames. If chunk boundary lands inside a JSON token we can mitigate by server-side framing (prefix length) or advising clients to buffer events until a full JSON object parse succeeds.
 customer_xyz: Quick test: curl --http1.1 --no-buffer -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -N 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream' > out.txt
 Result: no truncation in 20 runs. HTTP/2 shows failure 6/10.
 tara_infra: That smells like an HTTP/2 frame boundary issue combined with the client's service worker doing a midstream socket replacement. Two mitigation paths: 1) short-term: advise customer to use HTTP/1.1 for long-lived structured streams. 2) longer: make server assemble SSE events server-side with guaranteed event-atomic boundaries (we already send `data: ` per event but we can add an event checksum or length prefix as opt-in).
 mike_eng: Also check billing/auth: if a token rotation triggers a new request that increments usage counters or starts a new billing event, we should ensure partials don't get counted as final. @eve_support can you flag billing to ignore partial streams that end with connection reset?
 eve_support: Filed billing ticket INC-2468 to review usage attribution for aborted streams.
 customer_xyz: For now our workaround is to buffer events and only parse when we see matching braces. But we need a robust fix. Any ETA on server-side framing?
 mike_eng: I'll open an infra PR to add an optional \"event-length\" header inside the SSE payload for structured mode so clients can validate complete payloads. Tentative: v0.12.3 runtime patch, roll canary next week.
 tara_infra: We'll also add extra logging to edge proxies to correlate HTTP/2 stream resets with auth refreshes.
 eve_support: Summarizing action items: 1) Customer to keep using HTTP/1.1 or buffer client-side (temporary). 2) Eng to prototype event-length framing + edge logs. 3) Billing to review aborted stream attribution. 4) Support to monitor customer until canary.
 customer_xyz: Thanks — appreciate quick triage. Please CC me on the PR/patch so we can test canary.
 mike_eng: Will do. @customer_xyz please share a short sample curl/trace when you can. Also include service worker code if possible.
 ci_deploybot: note: canary window scheduled for 1969999600-1969999800, will post updates in #eng-releases.
 customer_xyz: got it, thanks all :thumbsup:
 mike_eng: One last note — we should update docs to recommend HTTP/1.1 for long-lived structured SSE until framing is live. I'll file a docs PR after the infra patch. :eyes:
